purpose: Hydralazine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower your blood pressure to reduce the risk of heart attacks, strokes, and kidney problems. It may also be used in certain heart failure patients, often alongside other medications.
how_it_works: Your blood vessels can sometimes tighten up, which makes your heart work harder and raises your blood pressure. Hydralazine works by relaxing and widening the walls of your blood vessels, especially the arteries. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down.
common_side_effects: Headache, dizziness, fast or pounding heartbeat (palpitations), flushing (feeling warm or red in the face), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, and swelling in the legs or feet are the most common side effects. These often improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you develop joint pain, muscle aches, a skin rash, or feel like you have flu-like symptoms — this could be a rare condition called drug-induced lupus. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as your blood pressure could spike. Use with caution if you have heart disease, kidney disease, or a history of stroke. Let your doctor know all other medications you take, as some can interact with hydralazine.
typical_dosing: Adults usually start with 10 mg taken by mouth 4 times a day. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose up to 200–300 mg per day depending on how your blood pressure responds. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, and try to take it at the same times each day.
